A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnyIR, with matchable algorithms, experiments and figures. All supplied pages are readable, including v2 Appendices A-F. v1 ends with references despite mentioning separate supplementary material; newly supplied appendix content is assessed as newly documented evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration experiments, unseen and mixed-degradation evaluations, efficiency measurements, component ablations and feature analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original restoration experiments and reports additional underwater evaluation, model variants, ablations, data-balancing results and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The skip-split architecture, attention pathway, GatedDA and spatial-frequency fusion procedure remain substantially unchanged. As written, Algorithm 1 adds a small constant delta inside the standard-deviation square root. Newly disclosed losses and the learnable fusion weight do not establish changes from v1's unspecified implementation choices.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot underwater enhancement on UIEB, extending evaluation to a distinct real-world domain. Its CDD11 comparison also expands from two triple-degradation scenarios in v1 Table 5 to eleven single, double and triple combinations in v2 Table 3. The principal three- and five-degradation benchmarks and unseen CSD evaluation remain.

E2.justification: The main three- and five-degradation comparator sets remain. However, the CDD11 comparison adds WGWSNet and WeatherDiff and removes TransWeather; CSD adds MoCE-IR-S, and the complexity comparison adds full-sized MoCE-IR. v1's extensive single-task comparison table disappears, although its PromptIR/AnyIR deraining comparison survives in v2's capacity analysis.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include Tiny/Small configurations, depth and prompt controls, fusion-weight alternatives, and training-data rebalancing using approximately 90% of the original samples. Appendix A specifies evaluating the five-degradation checkpoint on 890 UIEB images without fine-tuning. These are additional experimental designs; newly disclosed settings alone do not establish changes to retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds capacity and prompt-removal controls in Table 9, spatial-only versus frequency-only versus fixed/learnable fusion in Table 10, and data-distribution sensitivity in Table 12. Appendix B adds PCA and t-SNE representation analyses. The earlier component ablations, channel-activation analysis and SVD analysis remain, rather than constituting new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report unexplained plus/minus quantities for FLOPs, without run counts, seeds, restoration-score uncertainty or significance tests. v2 changes these values and adds rows but does not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces AnyIR's 32.83 dB average with 32.80/32.86 for Tiny/Small. Table 2 revises PromptIR's average from 29.15 to 29.72 dB. Table 6 replaces AnyIR's 6.29M parameters/19G FLOPs with 5.74M/26G and 8.51M/39G configurations. Numerous underwater, CDD11, ablation and timing results are added, while most single-task entries disappear. These are not established same-setting gains. v2 Table 2 reports Tiny's average as 30.71, although its five scores average approximately 30.55.

T1.justification: New Section 3.1 explicitly defines the degradation observation model and four encoder-decoder mapping paradigms, adding a limited mathematical formulation of the problem and architectural distinctions. No theorem, proof or formal generalization guarantee is added; the principal attention and fusion equations are retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains efficient, unified restoration without external prompts. The abstract revises parameter/FLOP savings from approximately 82%/85% to 84%/80%. The conclusion more explicitly restricts the model's scope to degradations covered by current all-in-one benchmarks, refining the earlier broad 'any image' framing.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a multi-environment, degradation-invariant representation interpretation and connects training-distribution balance to the learned reconstruction prior. Appendix E adds substantive limitations concerning globally uniform corruption, degradation concentrated in one domain, and reduced global-modeling flexibility. It explicitly excludes unrestricted restoration of arbitrary degradations; v1 primarily discussed component complementarity and dataset imbalance.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Table 11 supply dataset counts, training budgets, Adam settings, loss descriptions, crops, augmentation, batch size, GPUs and explicit Tiny/Small configurations largely absent from the supplied v1 PDF. Code availability changes from promised to stated available. These improve documentation without proving implementation changes. Reproducibility remains limited by conflicting epoch counts between A.1 and A.2.

R1.justification: Sections 2-3.1 substantially expand positioning through four architectural paradigms, multi-environment learning, and explicit comparison with expert routing. New references include the Jiang et al. survey, Tang et al.'s unified restoration work and Perceive-IR; numerous single-task and peripheral references disappear. Publication updates to retained works are not treated as new citations.

P1.justification: The introduction and method explanation are substantially rewritten around inverse problems and degradation-invariant learning. The former method overview becomes separate preliminaries and framework subsections, experimental organization changes, and appendices organize protocols, analyses, additional results, limitations and broader impact. These constitute extensive narrative restructuring beyond simply adding experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column conference layout to a single-column journal layout. The overview moves from Figure 1 to Figure 4, and retained figures are resized or rearranged. New diagrams, underwater examples and appendix visualizations appear; the CDD11 table expands to eleven scenarios, and tables gain model-variant rows and second-best highlighting.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central efficiency and generalization argument: Appendix A supplies previously missing implementation information, Tables 9-10 test capacity and fusion alternatives, and expanded CDD11/UIEB evaluations and Appendix E better establish applicability and boundaries. These gains outweigh the loss of most single-task comparisons and reporting defects, notably the incorrect Tiny average in Table 2, stale five-degradation discussion and conflicting epoch counts. Those defects limit confidence in exact figures, but the added validation and documentation materially improve the paper's assessability.
